title: orchestration-checklist-timeline-preflight-jun-2026
content:
Purpose: This doc is the working preflight + orchestration checklist, condensed rollout calendar, and a first-cut release notes draft for the 2026-06 feature deployment. It consolidates tasks for release engineering, SRE, product, and customer success. Use as the single source during the release window; keep it updated live during handoffs.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to hosted API and Dedicated clusters only for this push; Private deployments are opt-in and will follow separate distro docs.
- Non-breaking by default, but includes an optional model-refresh that may affect latency profiles for long-context paths.
- Primary deploy window targeted: 2026-06-16 to 2026-06-18 (UTC). Canary-first, progressive regional rollout.

High-level owners (quick reference):
- Release lead: Priya Menon (release engineering)
- SRE on-call: Riley Thompson
- Runtime owner (kernel/compilation): Liam Chen
- Product PM: Sofia Ruiz
- CS lead (customer comms): Amir Patel

Key objectives for this release:
1) Ship continuous-batching improvements that reduce p50 token latency by ~6% on N5 instances.
2) Add an alternator routing policy for fallback under GPU contention.
3) Update model catalog metadata and add quantization metadata fields.

Preflight checklist (must be green before starting canary):
- [ ] All merged PRs have CI pass and no outstanding security reports. (owner: Priya) 
- [ ] Release branch cut and CI build available in artifacts; build SHA recorded. (owner: Liam)
- [ ] Staging smoke test: text-gen, streaming, embeddings, function call integrations pass (sanity token budget, warmup sequences). (owner: Riley)
- [ ] Canary images pushed to registry and signed. (owner: release-engineering automation)
- [ ] Canary routing policy ready with immediate rollback hook (owner: Liam)
- [ ] KPI dashboard panels created: token latency p50/p95, inference errors/sec, rate-limited responses, GPU mem pressure, queue length. (owner: observability)
- [ ] Runbook links populated in PagerDuty escalation and Slack shortcuts. (owner: SRE)
- [ ] Customer advisory drafted and reviewed for potential latency impact. (owner: CS)
- [ ] Legal/security checklist: third-party libs scanned and approved. (owner: security)
- [ ] Backfill/telemetry for new fields in model catalog validated in data pipeline. (owner: data-platform)

Release week calendar (compact):
D-7 (2026-06-09):
- Stabilize all blocking PRs, freeze merges to main branch except fixes.
- QA runbooks and end-to-end scenarios executed on staging cluster.

D-3 (2026-06-13):
- Final customer comms review; schedule advisory for noon UTC on D-1.
- Begin pre-deploy warmups on canary pool (low traffic).

D-1 (2026-06-15):
- Morning: run full-system smoke tests on a fresh staging image. Sign-off meeting 11:00 UTC (release lead + SRE + PM).
- 15:00 UTC: Freeze non-critical database migrations and schema changes.
- 18:00 UTC: Push canary image to registry and mark for deployment.

D0 (2026-06-16) Canary stage:
- 00:00 UTC: Start canary at 1% traffic in us-east and europe-west. Verify immediate health checks. (owner: Riley)
- 00:30 UTC: Run synthetic load for 5 minutes at 2x baseline to detect mem pressure.
- 01:00 UTC: Evaluate KPIs (p50/p95 latency, error rates) for 30 minutes. If metrics are green -> advance.
- 04:00 UTC: Expand to 5% traffic and add ap-southeast region at 1%.
- 08:00 UTC: If stable for 4 hours, move to slow rollout.

Slow rollout (D0 continued):
- 12:00 UTC: Increase to 15% traffic; monitor for model-related regressions (incorrect tokenization edge cases).
- 18:00 UTC: 40% traffic if stable. Prepare communications for teams and a short all-hands release update.

Regional finalization (D1-D2, 2026-06-17 to 2026-06-18):
- D1 morning: 70% traffic, keep US and EU ahead of APAC.
- D1 evening: 90% traffic.
- D2 morning: 100% roll to hosted API; Dedicated pools auto-apply policy if configured by customers.

Post-release window (D2-D3):
- Monitor for 48 hours full telemetry retention. Trigger quality-monitoring alerts for any regressions tied to eval prompt sets.
- Collect user-facing metrics and CS feedback; schedule postmortem if any P1/P0 incidents.

Canary progression decision criteria (simple pass/fail):
- Pass: no increase > 2x in 5xxs, p95 latency <= baseline + 15%, GPU mem pressure < 80%, queue length stable.
- Fail: sustained error-rate increase, memory OOMs, or unexplainable latency spikes -> immediate rollback to previous image.

Rollback procedure (short):
1) Flag rollback in Slack (#release-coord-2026-06) and trigger PagerDuty. (owner: release lead)
2) Switch routing at the edge to previous stable image using routing controller (automated, 2-minute grace). (owner: runtime)
3) Scale canary down to 0% and validate health on stable image for 15 minutes. (owner: SRE)
4) Post-rollback postmortem within 72 hours, assign action owners.

Monitoring playbook (what to watch):
- Inference errors/sec (alerts at >5/min sustained)
- p95 end-to-end token latency by route (alerts if > baseline+15%)
- GPU kernel failure metrics and driver restarts
- Autoscaler thrashing and queue depth spikes
- Function-calling regression rates and malformed outputs
- Billing/quota anomalies (unexpected token increase)

Communications templates (short forms):
- Slack announcement (internal): "Release D0: starting canary at 00:00 UTC. Watching latency p50/p95 closely. Ping @release-oncall for issues. Canary SHA: <sha>"
- External customer advisory (CS): "Planned maintenance: We will deploy performance and routing improvements starting 2026-06-16. No expected downtime; minor latency variance possible. Contact support if you see regressions."

Release notes draft (to be expanded):
- Summary: Rolling out continuous-batching and a new fallback routing policy to improve inference stability and reduce latency.
- Features:
  - Continuous batching kernel improvements (N5 optimized) — expected ~6% p50 reduction.
  - Alternator routing policy: automatic fallback to compatible model variants under GPU pressure.
  - Model catalog metadata: quantization fields and latency profiles now available via API.
- Bug fixes:
  - Fix memory leak in KV cache population for long-context sequences.
  - Addressed incorrect stream flush leading to partial function-call outputs.
- Notes for operators:
  - No required customer action for hosted customers. Dedicated customers can opt into the new routing policy via console or API.
  - If you maintain private deployments, see Confluence page for the on-prem upgrade checklist.

Post-release validation checklist (owners in parens):
- [ ] Validate 48-hour error rate parity vs baseline (observability)
- [ ] Confirm CS has zero escalations within 24 hours (CS)
- [ ] Confirm billing anomalies none or explainable (finance)
- [ ] Run regression evals on the canonical prompt set (applied-ml)

Unresolved questions / open items:
- Q1: Should we auto-enable alternator routing for Dedicated customers without prompting? (Sofia to decide by D-1)
- Q2: Telemetry volume increase: need retention guarantees if new model-metadata doubles event payload (data-platform to estimate).
- Q3: If APAC region shows slower kernel warmup, do we delay full rollout for APAC only? (Ops decision tree needed)

Notes to self / quick todos before finalizing:
- Add exact SHA and artifact links after build completes.
- Formalize postmortem template and link in runbook.
- Add brief script list for synthetic tests used during canary (Riley).

Appendix: quick command snippets (placeholders)
- Force rollback (example): curl -X POST https://ops-api.redwood.ai/v1/route-switch -d '{"target":"stable","reason":"rollback"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>'
- Canary expansion toggle: gh workflow run canary-toggle.yml --ref <sha> --input percent=5

End of working draft. Keep this doc updated in real time during the release window. After the release, convert to a permanent runbook and publish to Confluence with final metrics and postmortem summary.
